task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-07-13, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies within team, is separable from talent/counts, and talent control behaves.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 420,993 possessions; 90 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: How to measure lineup coverage from player role categories
How to isolate within-team coverage variation from roster composition and player counts
How to control for overall talent without circularity
What confounding factors affect the estimated effect of coverage on offensive efficiency
How to verify that talent control behaves as expected
evidence_establishes: Role categories (Primary Organizer, Shaper, Terminal Scorer) can be assigned per player per team-season using initiation and structural influence as defined in prior project work
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether lineup coverage (>=1 organizer, shaper, terminal) varies meaningfully within a team
Whether any such variation is separable from simply counting high-usage players or from aggregate talent metrics
That talent control variables behave stably and predictably when testing a coverage hypothesis
Any previous design or pilot results specific to lineup coverage
own_inferences: The required data (per-game play-by-play, substitution intervals, player-level initiation records) is sufficient to compute structural fingerprints and role categories for each team-season
Lineup coverage can be defined as a binary stent-level variable: a stint has coverage if the five players on court together include at least one Primary Organizer, one Shaper, and one Terminal Scorer

Within-team variation is possible only if the team roster contains at least one player of each category and the rotation sometimes places them on the bench together; if all lineups always have coverage there is no variation to test

Separability from talent/counts can be tested by adding aggregated player talent (offensive EPM or RAPM) and simple counts of each role category on the floor to a regression of stint-level points per possession on coverage
'Talent control behaves' likely means that the talent coefficient is positive, stable across model specifications, and does not change sign erratically when coverage is included
uncertainties: The distribution of role categories across rosters and lineups; some teams may have no Shaper, making coverage impossible by definition, or may always field all three roles
Stability of role assignments across a season; roles are derived from full-season usage and influence which could introduce endogeneity if the same games are used for the coverage test
The appropriate talent metric and whether a single-number summary (e.g., sum of offensive EPM) adequately captures the skill components most relevant to coverage
The minimal stint length needed for reliable PPP estimation and the resulting effective sample size
Whether the mechanical requirement of needing at least three distinct role players creates a floor effect that confounds interpretation of coverage coefficients

historical_effect.explanation: No prior study on this specific question was returned, so the decision is based entirely on data availability, conceptual reasoning, and risk assessment.

blocking_constraints.text: Within-team variation in coverage may be rare if most lineups naturally contain at least one organizer, shaper, and terminal. If the proportion of stints lacking coverage is very low, statistical power to detect an effect will be insufficient.

Player role categories depend on usage and residual structural influence thresholds. For players near the median or with few initiations, classification can be noisy, leading to misclassification of coverage status.

The coverage definition requires at least three specific role players on the floor. If a team roster lacks any of those roles entirely, all stints are uncovered by construction, eliminating variation. Even when roles exist, natural substitution patterns may enforce a coverage floor.

Role categories are correlated with player skill; shapers and organizers tend to be better players. Controlling for talent with a single metric may leave residual confounding, making it difficult to isolate pure 'coverage' from general player quality.

prior_work.summary: No earlier project study on lineup coverage was retrieved. The role framework exists and is operational, but the specific hypothesis has not been tested.

risks.text: Limited within-team variation in coverage may render estimates imprecise or inestimable.
Role misclassification attenuates the coverage signal and can bias coefficients.
If roles are defined using the same games in which coverage is tested, extreme role realizations may regress, creating spurious associations.
Role categories are derived from initiation patterns that are part of the offensive efficiency measure; using them as regressors risks circularity unless roles are estimated from prior data.
Omitted variable bias from unmeasured aspects of player skill or coach strategy may confound the coverage effect.
Teams with very imbalanced rosters may never achieve coverage, and those that always have it offer no variation; the floor effect complicates inference.
Testing coverage across many team-seasons inflates the chance of false positives unless adjusted.
Role categories may shift over the season due to player development, injuries, or coaching changes, violating the assumption of static roles.

design.estimand: The causal effect of stent-level lineup coverage (binary: >=1 Primary Organizer, >=1 Shaper, >=1 Terminal Scorer) on offense-only points per possession (PPP), controlling for aggregated player talent and the counts of each role type present.
design.unit: Stint (continuous interval of fixed ten players), filtered to a minimum of 3 possessions and excluding garbage time.
design.sample: All regular-season stints from NBA 2022-23 through 2025-26. Separate secondary analyses for playoffs and for first-vs-second half to check consistency.
design.power: Simulation-based power analysis using 2022-23 to 2024-25 data: estimate the intra-team standard deviation of coverage status, compute the minimum detectable effect size (MDES) for a within-team partial correlation at 80% power, and proceed only if MDES is plausible (e.g., < 0.02 PPP). If within-team variation is too scarce, pool teams in a hierarchical model and report MDES for the overall average effect.
design.controls: Game- and quarter-fixed effects, point differential at stint start (binned), sum of offensive EPM or multi-year RAPM for the five offensive players, and count of each role category present (organizers, shapers, terminals). A robustness check adds interactions between talent and role counts.
design.falsification: 1) Role-permutation placebo: randomly reassign roles within each team-season 10,000 times and check that the true coverage coefficient lies outside the 95th percentile of the null distribution. 2) Test the coverage effect on defensive PPP, where no mechanism predicts a positive effect; any finding there would suggest residual talent confound. 3) Garbage-time validation: coverage effect should attenuate in garbage time if it reflects strategic coherence.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register a single primary hypothesis test on the average coverage coefficient from a hierarchical Bayesian model with team-level random slopes. Report team-specific effects with 95% credible intervals after applying a Benjamini-Hochberg correction across teams as an exploratory output.
design.decision_rule: Coverage is judged separable from talent if its posterior probability of being positive exceeds 0.975 after controlling for talent and role counts, and if the talent coefficient remains positive and stable (no sign reversal across 95% of posterior draws) across all pre-registered model specifications. 'Talent control behaves' is verified if the talent coefficient's sign aligns with prior knowledge and its inclusion does not flip the coverage coefficient's sign.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files as of 2026-07-13, play-by-play and substitution data, with player-level structural fingerprints and roles derived from the project graph database using the 2022-23 through 2025-26 seasons.
